short_answer: Danny's VIP Sports Picks is a real seller in the narrow sense that it has a live CapperTek listing, posts picks there most days and sells access at published prices. The seller gives no full name, company, address or website of its own, so a buyer knows very little about who is behind it.

The good news for a buyer is that a full pick log exists. CapperTek records each pick with the time it was entered, the odds and the stake, and grades it. The bad news is what the log shows. On 20 Nov 2026 CapperTek put the five year window at 939 wins, 850 losses and 12 pushes, about 52% winners, for -179.20 units and a -2.09% return. That is 46 units worse than on 7 Nov 2026, after a bad November. We counted all 1,806 logged picks ourselves and got the same totals.

The log does show one real strength: baseball. His MLB straight bets are up about 68 units. Hockey parlays and hockey in general have cost far more than that. Treat Danny as a cheap seller whose own record is losing overall, not as a proven winner. A cheap pick that loses still costs you the bet.
pricing_intro: Prices below were shown on the CapperTek purchase tab for DannysVIPSportsPicks.cappertek.com on 20 Nov 2026, the same as on 7 Nov 2026. CapperTek says sellers set their own prices and are paid through their own PayPal account, and it charges sellers no commission. A buyer must register a free CapperTek customer account to buy.
pricing: Handicapper's picks for 1 day. No refund terms shown on the listing
guarantee: We found no guarantee of any kind on the Danny's VIP listing. The bio promises how picks are delivered, not results: it says "YOU WILL RECEIVE EACH PICK AT LEAST 25 MINUTES BEFORE GAME TIME".

CapperTek's terms of service say that "all fees and charges (including subscription fees) are non-refundable" unless otherwise stated, and that payment on provider sites goes through PayPal. Nothing on the listing states otherwise. A buyer with a problem would have to go to the seller, whose contact details CapperTek shows only to logged in customers, or to PayPal. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered by any pick seller.

claims_note: How we checked: CapperTek publishes the whole pick history for this listing as one page. On 20 Nov 2026 we read every entry, 1,806 picks from 25 Sep 2023 to 19 Nov 2026, and added up the results, stakes and times ourselves. Our totals matched CapperTek's own chart exactly: 939 wins, 850 losses, 12 pushes (plus 5 voided picks) and -179.20 units. The MLB and NHL charts also matched our sport splits, so the numbers below come from the log itself, not from marketing.

By year the log reads: 2023 (from late Sep) 82-109-2, -80.32 units; 2024 178-170-5, -12.90 units; 2025 281-211, +22.95 units; 2026 so far 398-360-5, -108.93 units. 2025 was the one winning year. November 2026 has been poor: 21-29-1 for -86.39 units through 19 Nov, and 14-20-1 for -48.97 units since our first check on 7 Nov 2026.

Baseball is the strength. MLB straight bets went 336-235-2 for +67.98 units, and the MLB chart on CapperTek, which includes parlays, shows 362-289-2 and +35.32 units over five years. A reviewer in Aug 2026 said Danny was locked in on baseball, and the log backs that up for the period: MLB picks from 1 Jul to 13 Aug 2026 went 77-51 for +72.55 units.

Hockey and parlays are the weakness. The CapperTek NHL chart shows 209-181-3 and -175.06 units, a -9.64% return. NHL parlays alone went 6-31 for -112.09 units. Across all sports, parlays went 82-181 for -151.42 units, while straight bets went 857-669-12 for -27.78 units, close to break even on 7,543 units risked.

Win rate and profit point in different directions because many plays are favorites. Of 1,543 straight picks with the odds shown, 484 were priced at -150 or shorter and 183 at -200 or shorter, against 198 underdogs. Laying -200 needs a win rate of about 67% just to break even.
record: Independently checkable: CapperTek, a pick marketplace that says it charges sellers "Zero fees or commissions", keeps a documented record for this listing. Each pick shows the game, the side, the odds, the stake in units, the time the pick was made and the time it was graded, and picks are revealed to the public 30 minutes after the game starts. Its record windows on 20 Nov 2026 read: last 90 days 62-55-1, -64.85 units, -7.77%; last 180 days 202-164-2, -11.59 units, -0.51%; last 365 days 440-397-5, -126.41 units, -2.74%; last 730 days 699-586-5, -72.71 units, -1.06%; last 1,825 days 939-850-12, -179.20 units, -2.09% on 8,584.8 units risked. CapperTek says ROI is based on a $100 per unit risk amount.

Ranking: the CapperTek leaderboard for the last 30 days listed 231 handicappers on 20 Nov 2026. Danny's VIP was at 38-43-1 for -103.09 units and a -17.18% return, which put it 205th of 231 by units. 104 listings were in profit over the same 30 days.

Limits of that log: the seller enters his own picks, and CapperTek is a directory and marketplace, not an auditor. We cannot see whether every pick sent to paying customers appears in it, or whether customers got the same odds. There are gaps with no picks at all, such as Jun to Sep 2024, Mar 2025 and Sep 2026.

Seller marketing: the bio and reviews speak of consistent winning and a top win percentage. Those are claims; the numbers above are the log. We found no court or regulator action involving this seller in our searches, and with no legal name given there was nothing further to search.

customers_intro: All the buyer evidence we found sits on one site: seven short reviews on the seller's CapperTek page, all positive, from five usernames, one of which posted three times. On 20 Nov 2026 there were still seven, the newest from 13 Aug 2026. We found nothing on BBB, Reddit or the betting forums. Below, each review sits next to what the seller's own log showed for the same period.

customers.text: Every buyer comment we could find about Danny's VIP Sports Picks is positive, and every one sits on the CapperTek listing that sells the picks. There are seven reviews from five usernames, posted between Feb 2024 and Aug 2026; one username wrote three of them, and two others arrived on the same day in Mar 2024. Reviewers praise the low price, the small number of daily picks, quick wins in hockey and basketball and, most often, baseball. None posts a record. Where a review names a period, the seller's own log sometimes supports it (baseball in summer 2026 was strongly profitable) and sometimes does not (an 80% NFL claim against a logged 57%, and a "best winning percentage" claim when the log stood near 53%). Searches of BBB, Reddit archives, Covers, SBR and TheRX found no independent post, positive or negative, and no complaint about billing or refunds.

One username wrote three of the seven reviews. In Feb 2024 he said Danny had won him a lot of money that weekend in hockey and basketball and called baseball Danny's strength; in Aug 2026 he said Danny was locked in on baseball with one of the higher win percentages around. The log supports the 2026 baseball comment (77-51, +72.55 units from 1 Jul to 13 Aug 2026) and shows that weekend in Feb 2024 at 12-7 and +5.54 units, inside a month that finished 37-34-1 and -22.32 units.

A reviewer said Danny should be ranked first because he has the best winning percentage, said the picks had made him a good amount of cash, and criticized handicappers who, in his words, pay for their top rankings. On the date of that review the seller's own log stood at 443-400-7, about 52.6% winners and -33.07 units.

A reviewer claimed the NFL picks hit 80% and praised the hockey and college basketball picks. He liked that Danny sends about two picks a day rather than seven and skips days with nothing he likes. The log shows NFL picks for that season at 17-13 (57%) and +27.39 units: profitable, but not 80%.

Two reviews arrived the same day. One buyer, referred by a friend and about a month in, said they could not seem to lose; the other said he only sticks with "a sure thing" and Danny had not disappointed. The log for the month before those reviews reads 45-36-1 and about +1 unit. No bet is a sure thing, and neither review gave a record.

BBB again returned no results for the name. Reddit archive searches of the main betting subreddits, web searches and site searches found no thread about this seller, and we found no TheRX, Covers or SBR discussion. The seller has no website of its own, so there was no Trustpilot or SiteJabber page to check.

conflicts: We saw no sportsbook affiliate links or promo codes on the seller's CapperTek pages. CapperTek's own footer lists Pinnacle and FanDuel as partners; that is the marketplace, not the seller.

The listing carries a CapperTek "Verified Service" label. CapperTek's FAQ says verified means the service placed a verification banner on its website and opened a line of communication so CapperTek can resolve complaints. It is not a check of results. CapperTek separately sells Pro Featured placement for a monthly advertising fee.
Reviews on CapperTek are anonymous and user submitted, and CapperTek says it does not guarantee their accuracy. The seller replies to several of them, and a buyer cannot tell who wrote them.
strengths: A full public, time stamped pick log with odds and stakes, graded by the platform. We could recount all 1,806 picks and our totals matched CapperTek's.
Low prices: $10 for a day or $120 for 30 days, about $4 a day.
Baseball has been genuinely profitable in the log: MLB straight bets are up about 68 units since Sep 2023.
Straight bets overall are close to break even (-27.78 units on 7,543 risked), so a buyer who skips the parlays would have lost far less.
Few picks a day by the seller's and one reviewer's account, which makes the plays easy to track.
concerns: The seller's own CapperTek log is negative over 90 days, one year, two years and five years, despite a bio that claims consistent winning.
Parlays, especially NHL parlays, have lost heavily: 82-181 for -151.42 units across all sports.
One in eight picks was entered less than 25 minutes before the listed start, against the bio's 25 minute promise.
Stakes run from 1 to 11 units, and the biggest plays (8 units or more) lost 74 units, so a cold run can cost a follower a lot quickly.
No name, company, address or website, and no refund terms beyond CapperTek's rule that fees are non refundable.
All customer reviews come from one site, five usernames and no records.
checklist: Open the CapperTek picks tab, set it to the last 365 days and the last 1,825 days, and read the units, not the win rate.
Filter by sport. Baseball and hockey tell very different stories in this log.
Decide in advance whether you will follow the parlays. In this log they lost far more than the straight bets.
Bet a flat stake of your own rather than copying 8 to 11 unit plays.
Write down each pick the moment you receive it, with the time and the odds you can actually get, and compare with the log.
Remember the CapperTek terms: fees are non refundable, so buy the shortest pass first.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: Is Danny's VIP Sports Picks legit?

It is a real, active CapperTek seller that posts picks and sells access at published prices, and every pick is logged with time and odds. The seller gives no name, company or address, and its own logged record does not show the consistent winning its bio claims.
How much does Danny's VIP Sports Picks cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 CapperTek listed $10 for 1 day, $50 for 7 days, $75 for 14 days, $120 for 30 days and $220 for 60 days. We found no refund terms, and CapperTek's terms say fees are non refundable unless stated.
Does Danny's VIP Sports Picks have a verified record?

It has a CapperTek documented record with pick times, odds and stakes, which anyone can read, though the seller enters the picks and CapperTek is not an auditor. On 20 Nov 2026 it showed 939-850-12 and -179.20 units over the last 1,825 days, and our own count of all 1,806 picks matched. Watchdog has no graded record of its own.
Which sports does Danny do best in?
Baseball. MLB straight bets in the log went 336-235-2 for +67.98 units. Hockey is the weak spot: the NHL chart shows -175.06 units, much of it from parlays.
Does Danny send picks early enough to bet?

Usually, but not always. Most picks are entered hours before the start, yet 242 of 1,806 logged picks were entered less than 25 minutes before the listed start time, and 91 less than 10 minutes before.
Is Danny's VIP Sports Picks worth it?

For the money you get a few cheap daily picks across baseball, hockey, basketball and football. What is unproven is any long run profit: the seller's own log is down 179.20 units over five years, so a buyer would be paying for picks that have not beaten the market over time, apart from baseball.
